content.thinking:
I'm noticing a timing mismatch — the candidate claims the flag toggled between 09:15 and 09:16, but the record shows the change at 09:20:47, after the onset, while the log at 09:15 already shows a mix of on/off evaluations, suggesting the flag was partially active earlier than the candidate's account implies.

I'll avoid committing to specific percentage figures like a 0% to 100% rollout since those aren't confirmed. Then I want to build out the causal chain: requests to the account page failed, tracing back to a ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47, which only triggers under a specific monthly-spend condition.

For contributing factors, I'm thinking through what should be flagged as preventable: the flag being enabled without a validated code path (fixable with a zero-case test and pre-enable check), and the absence of automatic rollback tied to error-rate spikes for flag changes. I also want to note the gap between onset and when the alert fired, as a detection gap worth calling out — while being careful not to assert specific numeric values that aren't verified in the record.

action_items.item: Add a regression test for the zero-divisor case in the monthly spend summary code. Require it to pass before the pull request that fixes it is merged.

Add a pre-enable check for feature flags on the account page path. The flag's code path must pass tests against realistic account data, including zero values, before it can be switched on in production.
Roll flags out gradually. Have the flag provider automatically turn a flag off when the error rate on the affected service rises above baseline soon after the change.
Alert on a rise in account page errors, or on the first appearance of a new exception type, within a short time of a flag change. This would page sooner than the overall error-rate rule did.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers loading the account page got errors. The error rate rose from {errors_before} to {errors_while_broken} on average and reached {errors_at_worst} at worst, and the service logged repeated account page error-rate warnings.

Account page requests failed with a ZeroDivisionError (division by zero) in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, the monthly spend summary code. This error repeated from the onset until the end of the incident window.

That code ran because monthly-spend-feature began evaluating as on for traffic from the onset. The evaluations at the onset were a mix of off and on, and later evaluations were all on. The error timing matches the flag becoming active.
An admin switched the flag on, and the change log records it as a flag toggle. Once the flag was on, the spend summary code was exposed to live account page traffic.

The spend summary code divides by a value that can be zero, and the flag exposed it to real traffic with no guard. The record does not show what the divisor is or why it is zero. Reverting the flag stopped the errors and returned the service to baseline, which confirms the flagged path was the fault.

contributing_factors.factor: The flagged code path went live without a test or guard for a zero divisor. The defect was only found by real shoppers hitting it, and the fix is still an unmerged draft.
Flag changes have no staged rollout with an automatic error-rate check. Turning the flag on exposed shoppers to the fault, and the flag stayed on until Argus reverted it.
Detection was slow. The alert was raised {alert_raised - began} after the onset, so shoppers saw errors for that long before anyone was paged.

input.executive_summary: For {duration}, from {began} to {recovered}, a share of shoppers could not load their account page on io-shop. The error rate was {errors_while_broken} on average and peaked at {errors_at_worst}, against {errors_before} beforehand. That is {errors_rise} of traffic failing that otherwise would not have. The cause was a new feature, the monthly spend summary, that was turned on with a feature switch. It contained a calculation error that made the account page fail. Argus found the switch in the change history and turned it off. The error rate returned to its baseline and the alert stopped firing. Argus held the incident for {held}. A draft fix has been proposed and is waiting for review.

got_lucky: The failure was limited to the account page code path and did not affect latency, CPU or memory, so the rest of the shop kept working.
The flag could be reverted instantly with no deploy, so the revert needed no code change.
went_well: Argus tied the leading candidate to the flag change and reverted the flag within moments of forming the candidate.
The revert was checked against the service's own metrics. It was only called confirmed once the service was back at baseline and the paging rule had stopped firing.
A draft fix pull request was opened right after mitigation.
went_wrong: The flag was switched on without any guard against the zero-divisor failure, so shoppers hit the error first.
The alert fired well after the onset, and the flag stayed on until Argus reverted it.
The change record's timestamp for the flag toggle comes after the onset shown in the metrics and logs, which makes the timeline harder to read.

input.root_cause: The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on, and the code it enables on the account page path in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py raises a ZeroDivisionError. Nothing checked that path before the flag went live, and nothing rolled the flag back when errors rose.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for a share of shoppers
